findings.summary: Deterministic sample checks for R1/R2/R3 claim milestone coverage in both M1 and M2, but M1 deliverables/exit criteria are foundation-only and do not implement recursive file discovery, static site output, or Markdown rendering; substantive capability appears in M2. This overstates trace coverage for the sampled requirements.

evidence.note: Sample check for R1 includes M1.
M1 deliverables are orchestrator/context/plugin ordering/test harness/security stub; no collector/parser/renderer implementation.
evidence.quote: Core Orchestrator ... Plugin API ... shared build-context schema ... dependency/ordering ... test harness ... Security-by-default renderer policy stub

evidence.note: M2 introduces collector, parser, and renderer needed for R1/R2/R3.
evidence.quote: File Collector plugin ... Markdown Parser plugin ... Renderer/Theme plugin ... CLI command surface

evidence.note: Sample check for R2 includes M1.
Sample check for R3 includes M1.

findings.summary: R3→AT3 relies on “selected Markdown flavor” but the flavor/link dialect decision remains an open question (Q1). As written, AT3 pass criteria can be ambiguous without pinning the flavor/extensions set first, weakening the sampled trace’s determinism.

evidence.note: AT3 references the selected Markdown flavor but does not define it here.
evidence.quote: Prepare notes ... and tables per the selected Markdown flavor. Build the site and visually compare rendered HTML output to expected formatting.

evidence.note: Blocking open question about Markdown flavor/link syntax remains unresolved.
evidence.quote: What Markdown flavor and internal link syntax should be supported for links/backlinks (CommonMark/GFM; ...)?
